metrics_label_half.attacker_methods_result: all 400 Bad Request at the httptools/llhttp parser, before ASGI - no series minted

round2_block_dispositions.claim: /metrics Prometheus exposition injection via percent-decoded scope['path'] f-strung into a label
round2_block_dispositions.proof: 7 crafted percent-encoded paths carrying complete forged series plus 7 attacker-chosen methods produced 0 forged series; grep for forged|route="cr"|route="ff"|777|999999 over the scrape: NO forged series present
round2_block_dispositions.mechanism: two independent defences - the route label is the matched route template or the single <unmatched> bucket so the decoded path never reaches a label at all, and _escape_label escapes backslash, double-quote and newline on whatever does
round2_block_dispositions.gate_lead_question_1: Is carriage return still unescaped? YES - _LABEL_ESCAPES covers \\, " and \n only, not \r, \x0c, \x0b or \x00. NOT REACHABLE: the only two label sources are route (template or <unmatched>) and method. Recorded as W-2, a latent hardening gap.
round2_block_dispositions.gate_lead_question_2: Is scope['method'] attacker-controlled? NO - all 7 non-standard method tokens including GE"T and GE\T were rejected 400 Bad Request by httptools/llhttp before ASGI. The method label is confined to llhttp's fixed known-method table, which contains no quote, backslash or control character.

round2_block_dispositions.claim: /metrics unbounded cardinality - 60,000 label values and +28.2 MB permanently retained from one keep-alive connection

proof_by_measurement.interpretation: +2 MB of transient allocator noise with the series count unchanged, so nothing is retained per path

round2_block_dispositions.gate_lead_question_1: Do _duration_counts / _duration_totals inherit the bound? YES - both are keyed (method, route_label(scope)) through the same route_label(), and the exposition confirms it empirically: the histogram shows the same three route values as the counters after the flood.
round2_block_dispositions.gate_lead_question_2: Does method re-open it? NO - non-standard method tokens are rejected 400 by the protocol layer and never reach the counter.

round2_refutation_refuted.conclusion: toFixed is cheap even at 100,001 digits. Round 2's evaluator-3 timed a linear operation and concluded the quadratic one was fine. The cost is entirely in the regex.

reachability.constructor_check: toQuantizedDecimal() checks isFinite() only; decimal.js default maxE is 9e15, so 1e1000000 is finite and accepted
reachability.worst_measured: an 8-byte input (1e100000) blocks the JavaScript main thread for 4088 ms
reachability.model_validated: the quadratic model predicted 4.1 s from the 32,000-digit datapoint and measured 4.088 s
reachability.sibling_independent_confirmation: an independent sibling instance measured format_ms=4074.9 for the 8-byte case (agrees to 0.4%) and format_ms=429463.7 - 7 minutes 9 seconds - for the 9-byte 1e1000000, confirming and quantifying round 2's 'did not finish in 100 s'
reachability.caller_path: MoneyText's prop type is Money | string and it calls Money.fromWire(money).format() on the string branch, so any untrusted string routed to that component freezes the main thread

round2_block_dispositions.severity_judgement: Real defect with a measured 7-minute worst case and no upstream bound, but NOT an acceptance-criterion failure: no group-A AC asserts anything about format()'s time complexity, so it does not move the functional verdict. Not currently exploitable end to end either - group A wires no fetch and no form into MoneyText, and the backend serializer emits bounded 2dp strings. Latent defect whose severity rises the moment the first real caller appears, which is group B. One-line fix either way: bound the digit count in toQuantizedDecimal, or group with a linear loop instead of a lookahead.

round2_warn_dispositions.detail: sanitise_context now scrubs int/bool values and mapping KEYS. Measured: aadhaar_int 234123412346 -> [REDACTED]; key 'pan-ABCDE1234F' -> 'pan-[REDACTED]'; absolute path -> [REDACTED]\\db.env; leaks NONE. A harmless numeric threshold stays an int, so the fix did not silently change the wire contract.

the mutation test proves both AC2 tests kill a broken install loop, so 'vacuous' overstates it. Real defects: (a) the property holds only at the instant configure_logging() returns - a logger created later is in loggerDict with no filter; (b) the docstring's non-vacuity claim is empirically false, since logging.Logger('unregistered-probe-logger') never enters loggerDict and is disjoint from the enumerated set. Impact bounded: with default propagation the root handler's own RedactionFilter still scrubs the record (measured: PAN leaked = False), so a real leak needs propagate=False or a private handler. AC2 as worded is satisfied; F002 passes. WARN.
_escape_label does not escape \r, \x0c, \x0b or \x00. No attacker-controlled label source can carry them (see B-1). Latent hardening gap.
